column9: Why does the first element in a covalent name skip the prefix 'mono'?
column14: Because there is never just one of it
column15: Because it is always a metal
column17: By convention — mono is only written on the second element
column28: By convention, mono is left off the first element (CO is carbon monoxide, not monocarbon monoxide).

column4: Covalent bonds and naming covalent compounds
column9: Fluorine shares electrons with hydrogen atoms until fluorine has a full outer level. What is the formula of the molecule?
column28: Fluorine has 7 valence electrons and needs 1 more. One hydrogen shares 1 electron with it: HF.

column4: Covalent bonds and naming covalent compounds
column9: Two nitrogen atoms bond to make N₂. What kind of bond holds them together?
column28: Each nitrogen has 5 valence electrons and needs 3 more, so the two atoms share 3 pairs: a triple bond.

column4: Covalent bonds and naming covalent compounds
column9: Use the prefix table. How many chlorine atoms are in one molecule of phosphorus pentachloride?
column28: Penta means 5, so phosphorus pentachloride (PCl₅) has 5 chlorine atoms.

column4: Covalent bonds and naming covalent compounds
column9: In this electron dot structure of N₂, what kind of bond is the one labelled A?
column28: Three lines between the atoms = three shared pairs = a triple bond.

column4: Covalent bonds and naming covalent compounds
column9: Name N₂O. (Both elements need a prefix.)
column28: 2 nitrogen = dinitrogen; 1 oxygen = monoxide. Dinitrogen monoxide.

column4: Covalent bonds and naming covalent compounds
column9: Which of these is a covalent compound?
column28: H₂O is made only of nonmetals (H and O), so it is covalent. The others have a metal and a nonmetal (ionic).

column4: Covalent bonds and naming covalent compounds
column28: 1 phosphorus (no mono on the first element) and 3 chlorine = trichloride. Phosphorus trichloride.

column4: Covalent bonds and naming covalent compounds
column9: How many electrons are shared in a single covalent bond?
column28: A single bond is one shared pair: 2 electrons.

column4: Covalent bonds and naming covalent compounds
column9: Give the formula for sulfur trioxide.
column28: Sulfur (1, no prefix) and trioxide (3 oxygen): SO₃.
